newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks inch up in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks inch up in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened high, then eased in cautious trade, in advance of key economic data to be released in the U.S. on Friday, brokers said.

"I'm optimistic on the outlook for the fourth quarter but the index is likely to move sideways in advance of tonight's CPI figures and probably until the 24th, said David Williamson, sales director at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd. The Federal Open Market Committee meets on September 24.
The Hang Seng Index advanced just 4.85 points to 11,256.57 in the first 30 minutes of trading. Turnover was a moderate HK$532.85 million.
Most brokers said that any small interest rate hike in the United States and Hong Kong had already been taken into account by investors.
"An interest rate hike (in Hong Kong) has been discounted and the political side still looks good, said Janet Gillies, sales executive at OCBC Securities Ltd.
"We're positive on the Hong Kong market," she said.

The property sector led the market in early trading. Henderson Land put on HK$0.75 to trade at a new intra-day of HK$62.50. Some investors were thought to be seeking the HK$1.00 cash bonus announced in addition to the HK$1.43 final dividend.
The finance sector, which has been the main thrust, powering the Hang Seng to current levels, was up 0.13 percent in early trade.

Rumours have circulating this week that market heavyweight HSBC was interested in taking over Australia-New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ), said one broker. HSBC on Friday said it would not comment on the rumours.
Standard and Poor's upgraded ANZ's debt on Tuesday. ANZ is trading at A$6.78, off its 1996 high of A$6.90.
"HSBC has moved up after its good (interim results)" said Williamson. "We have a long-term target of HK$145.00 to HK$150.00 for the bank," he added.

New World Development advanced HK$0.30 to HK$38.50. The share, which has risen considerably in the past month, has caught the attention of those seeking property and China infrastructure exposure, analysts said.
The group's New World Infrastructure, which is viewed as an attractive China infrastructure play, rose HK$0.15 to HK$17.60,
CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.20 to trade at HK$33.40.
